text.p: Chiron Diagnostics on Tuesday unveiled its Rapidpoint 400 instant blood analysis machine -- describing it as a major breakthrough in intensive care decision-making.

The device -- resembling an electronic slot machine -- can at the touch of a screen icon produce within 60 seconds an analysis of a broad range of blood chemistry, marketing manager Christopher McNary told a news conference.
"With this instrument we have a fusion of two aims -- technology and economics," Joseph Keffer, Chief of Clinical Pathology at the University of Texas in Dallas, said.

He said that intensive care hospitals and clinics were being asked to produce better care with less money. Analytical laboratories were being centralised to cut costs, but the result was that it took longer for a doctor to get crucial information about a patient.
The new machine, he said, would give doctors key information at their fingertips in seconds.

Chiron Diagnostics -- a joint venture between Ciba Corning and the Chiron Corporation -- has operations in more than 20 countries, employs 3,500 people and in 1996 had worldwide sales of $684 million.
